briefs.source_chain: Systematic positioning is high with little incremental buying capacity left: BofA models systematics as net SELLERS in every scenario (sell $163bn down, sell $1bn flat, sell $9bn even in an up market); DB shows vol-control allocations maxed at the 100th percentile; GS corroborates with modest additional buying only if markets rise but a violent unwind if markets fall, with current systematic length ($146.5bn) at the upper end of its 1-year range -> separately, vol has collapsed to 'epic' compressed levels (McElligott), raising loss risk -> buybacks near peak just as the September blackout window expands, removing another buyer -> net message: incremental buying support is drying up from multiple directions just as vol is unusually compressed, a latent September unwind risk.
briefs.brief_chain: Systematic flows/buyback support becoming a headwind amid vol compression; states BofA sells $163bn in a down market but is BOUGHT $9bn in an up market; DB at 100th percentile; GS modest buying up/violent unwind down with length at upper end of range; McElligott calls vol collapse epic; buybacks near peak amid expanding blackout window.

distortions.what: Brief states BofA's model shows systematics '$9bn bought in an up market,' but the source has BofA modeling systematics as net SELLERS in an up market too (sell $9bn) — the note's whole point ('Sell sell or sell') is that BofA sees selling in all three scenarios, only the size varies.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — reading BofA as a net buyer in a rising market removes the one-sided/asymmetric selling risk that is the source's central thesis, understating how thin the offsetting-buyer support actually is if the tape rallies.

distortions.what: Brief's framing that the asymmetry is 'driven by positioning already being high rather than merely elevated' garbles the source's actual point, which is that the problem isn't the level of positioning per se but the lack of remaining incremental buying capacity.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — imprecise paraphrase, but it still lands on the correct overall conclusion (no room left to buy).
